title: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce - Business Studies - Types of Occupation
exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The legal and economic activity which a person engages in regularly in order to earn a living is referred to as an
questions.explain: An **occupation** refers to any legal and productive work, trade, or profession that an individual engages in on a daily basis to earn an income and satisfy their needs.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Occupations in a standard economy are broadly divided into four main categories. These are
questions.explain: The standard classification of occupations comprises four main divisions: **Primary** (extraction), **Industrial** (manufacturing/construction), **Commercial** (trade/distribution), and **Services** (direct/indirect).
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Occupations that involve the extraction and harvesting of raw materials directly from nature are classified as
questions.explain: **Primary occupations** deal directly with nature. Workers in this division extract raw materials from the land, sea, or air (e.g., farming, fishing, and mining).
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Which of the following professionals is engaged in a primary occupation?
questions.explain: A **coal miner** extracts coal directly from the earth, which is an extractive activity, placing them in the primary occupation category. Bricklayers are industrial, traders are commercial, and doctors are in services.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Industrial occupations are mainly concerned with
options: distributing goods to the final consumers
changing raw materials into finished or semi-finished goods
extracting crude oil from the ground
questions.explain: **Industrial occupations** (also known as secondary occupations) involve manufacturing and construction. They add value by processing raw materials (from primary occupations) into usable finished products.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A person whose daily job involves buying agricultural produce in bulk and selling it to market women belongs to the
questions.explain: Individuals who facilitate the distribution, buying, and selling of goods are engaged in trade, which is the core of **commercial occupations**.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The division of occupation that consists of people who perform intangible tasks to satisfy the needs of others rather than producing physical goods is called
questions.explain: The **services** occupation involves providing expertise, labor, or help (intangible actions) rather than physical commodities. Examples include teaching, nursing, and accounting.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Services as an occupation are subdivided into two categories. These are
questions.explain: Service occupations are structurally divided into two main groups based on who receives and pays for them: **direct services** and **indirect services**.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The main difference between direct and indirect services lies in
options: the level of education required to perform them
the physical location where the service is provided
who directly pays for the service rendered
whether the service involves physical goods or not
questions.explain: The distinguishing factor is **who pays**. Direct services are paid for by the individual receiving the service out of their own pocket, while indirect services are paid for by the government (using taxpayers' money) for the benefit of the general public.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Which of the following is a classic example of an individual providing a direct service?
options: A soldier defending the country's borders
A private home tutor teaching a student
A traffic warden directing vehicles on a public road
A judge passing a sentence in a government court
questions.explain: A **private home tutor** renders a direct service because the student's parents pay the tutor directly for the specific service provided to their child. The other options are paid for by the government (indirect).
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Indirect services are usually enjoyed by the general public and are paid for by the government. An example of a worker providing an indirect service is a
questions.explain: A **police officer** provides security to the general public, and their salary is paid by the state. Therefore, it is an indirect service.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: All of the following are factors that commonly affect a person's choice of occupation EXCEPT
options: natural resources available in their region
the color of their residential building
questions.explain: Educational background, potential salary (remuneration), and regional resources (e.g., coastal people choosing fishing) are all major factors influencing occupational choice. The **color of a building** is entirely irrelevant to economic choices.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: How does climatic condition act as a factor affecting occupation?
options: It strictly limits the amount of physical cash banks can hold.
It dictates the types of agricultural crops a farmer can cultivate.
It forces every individual in cold regions to become a factory worker.
It determines the school fees universities charge their students.
questions.explain: Climate affects primary occupations profoundly. It **dictates the types of crops a farmer can cultivate** (e.g., cocoa in rainy, tropical areas versus groundnuts in drier areas), thereby influencing their specific line of work.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: An occupation that falls under the "Commercial" division because it involves aids to trade is
questions.explain: Commercial occupations include both Trade and *Aids to Trade*. Since insurance facilitates trade, an **insurance broker** operates within a commercial occupation.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A person's natural talent or learned skill that determines how well they can perform a specific job is referred to in Business Studies as their
questions.explain: **Aptitude** refers to a person's natural ability, talent, or acquired skill, which acts as a major personal factor determining the type of occupation they choose or excel in.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies
